why: The question asks which C-C bond has the least inductive effect; the printed solution answers with a C-H bond ('the bond between carbon-3 and hydrogen'), so it does not answer its own question. The correct answer follows unambiguously from the book's OWN stated principle in the same solution - the effect diminishes as intervening bonds increase - applied to the two C-C bonds that exist: C1-C2 and C2-C3, of which C2-C3 is further from the bromine on C-1. A shipped worked example must not teach an answer of the wrong kind.
find: the effect is least in the bond between carbon-3 and hydrogen.
replace: the effect is least in the \(\text{C}_2-\text{C}_3\) bond — of the two \(\text{C}-\text{C}\) bonds present, it is the one further from the bromine on \(\text{C}_1\).
